newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: East Dries gold mine calm, output continues.
newsitem.headline: East Dries gold mine calm, output continues.

text.p: Driefontein Consolidated Ltd's east gold mine was calm on Monday and output was continuing after 18 miners were wounded in a clashes between rival groups at the weekend, Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said.
"It is calmer today (Monday) but not an awful lot of progress has been made. Production is continuing and there is a heavy police presence," a spokeswoman told Reuters.
Twenty-seven men were arrested during the fighting among workers from two hostel blocks at East Dries. Police said they would be charged with public violence and would appear in court on Monday.
A revolver, 15 rounds of ammunition and about 500 home-made weapons were seized when police broke up the clash.
Since July, at least 20 miners have died in feuding at Gold Fields' East Driefontein and Kloof Gold Mining Co mines.

The violence has been attributed to clashes between members of the 350,000-strong National Union of Mineworkers (NUM), which has a largely Xhosa membership on the mine, and the smaller, Zulu-led United Workers' Union of South Africa (Uwusa).
East Driefontein workers staged a five-day stayaway at the end of August, only returning to work on September 2.
Dries produced 11,680.6 kg of gold in the three months to end-June. Kloof produced 9,877.7 kg of gold in the June quarter. --Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
